relevance_note: Open-label taurine trial in SSADH deficiency giving per-patient data (age at enrollment, maximum dose, length of treatment) in Table 2: 'Eighteen patients provided follow-up data and were included in analysis'; no ALDH5A1 variant is printed for anyone.
method_note: Table 2 (columns: No., Age at enrollment y, Max dose mg/kg/d, Length of treatment mo, ABAS-II percentile changes) lists the 18 analysed patients by bare numbers, labelled 'Table 2 #n'; a short script transcribed rows 1-18 and I checked them against the table. Age at enrollment, max dose and length of treatment were put into treatment_summary because no individuals field holds age at enrollment; ages at onset, diagnosis and last evaluation are not given per person. ABAS-II changes were not recorded as features (they are scale changes, and minus signs appear lost in conversion, e.g. '20.05', '213.6'). Sex, race and age bands are given only as group counts (Table 1), so sex is 'not reported' per person. No ALDH5A1 variant or genotype is printed for any person, so the variants table is empty and n_patients_reported is null (the paper never states how many carry a variant); 25 enrolled patients is recorded as cohort_size_as_stated, of whom 7 without follow-up have no individual-level detail beyond group statements and get no rows. Possible duplicates inside the paper: the text says 'Sixteen unique subjects provided follow-up data' and that 'Two patients, females aged 17 and 19 years at initial enrollment, reenrolled in the trial after a 3-year hiatus', so the 18 Table 2 rows appear to represent 16 people, with two people listed twice; which rows cannot be determined (rows with age 17: #4 and #6; age 19: #7), so no rows were merged and no extra rows were created for these two women. The serious adverse event subject ('a subject (aged 30 years)' on 16 g/d, hospitalised for hypersomnia) cannot be matched to a Table 2 row (no age 30 in the table; may be a Table 2 patient at a later age or one of the 7 dropouts) and is recorded as 'unnamed person 1'; possible overlap with Table 2 #16 (28 y, 200 mg/kg/d, 50 mo) is not confirmed. Table 3 adverse effects are percentages without names and attribute nothing to anyone; the four individuals with social-domain improvement and the patients with large decreases are unnamed and not attributable. The previously published 2-year-old boy (reference 16, an abstract) is 'ref 16 patient'; '2-year-old' is not placed in an age field because it is unclear whether it is age at treatment start or at report. The reference's title mentions 'MRI-documented globus lesions' but the paper does not attribute them to the boy in its own text, so no MRI feature was recorded. clinical_diagnosis_basis is the study's stated basis for diagnosis ('when available genotype or enzymatic quantification'), applied to all trial subjects; it is not a per-person statement. Hypersomnia (an adverse event on taurine) was counted as 'sleep disturbances' on the checklist for unnamed person 1. No contradictions found.
